requests.purpose: Carry one tall communications tower, its camera head, its flag and its alert card through the film so the viewer follows what the camera sees, what it sends and what stays unmeasured.
requests.prompt: Author an original finished React and SVG object in the current Remotion engine. A tall riveted steel lattice communications tower with cross bracing and a small lopsided work platform near the top, an approximately 200 foot proportion with a rust drip and one leaning cable. At its top a weathered camera head with a rounded housing, a deep lens barrel, a sun hood, a heat shimmer ring and a sweep beam that rotates a full 360 degrees on the film clock. A small plume flag box that locks onto smoke with corner brackets, and one alert card, paper white with a worn corner and a drawn pin, that lifts off the head and travels. Late afternoon west Texas key light from the upper left with warm bounce, grounded contact shadows, hand made edges, nothing symmetric. A disclosed illustration with no real tower, logo, branding or site.
requests.source_limit: Disclosed illustration of the relationship AEP Texas describes. It does not show an AEP Texas tower, a real camera feed or a real smoke event, and it measures nothing.

requests.purpose: Give the tower a believable dry west Texas country and the working things that surround the alert: the row of cameras, the crew phone, the clock, the quiet calendar, the empty record card and the plan folder.
requests.prompt: Author an original finished React and SVG environment group in the current Remotion engine. Dry rolling west Texas country with mesquite, bunch grass, a caliche road, a windmill with a full disc fan and a swinging tail vane, a small plume that rises and leans in the wind, a utility truck cab with a dash, a crew phone with a masked text bubble, a row of fifty six tower slots of which sixteen light, a clock face with a ten minute arc, a launch calendar strip with no red mark, a blank response record card with an empty time field, a plan folder and a commission desk with an open stamp slot. Warm late light with cool fill, wear and dust, grounded shadows, nothing symmetric. No real logos, faces, names, phones or screens.
requests.source_limit: Disclosed illustration. The crew, truck and desk are anonymous stand-ins, the row shows AEP's own reported sixteen and plan of fifty six as slots rather than locations, and nothing here shows a county or a response time.

story_contract.opening_question: When a tower camera in west Texas sees smoke, what happens next?
story_contract.action: Put Pano AI cameras on communications towers in high-risk parts of its west Texas territory.
story_contract.change: A camera that watches all the way around flags heat or smoke, and software sends a text or an email to the AEP Texas team.
story_contract.affected_people: Residents and landowners in high-risk west Texas country, and the AEP Texas crews who receive the alert.
story_contract.consequence: AEP estimates the message arrives within ten minutes of detection, and says the cameras give situational awareness it can share with first responders.
story_contract.source_limit: Disclosed illustration of what AEP Texas's own page describes. Not an AEP Texas tower, a real camera feed, a real smoke event, a crew or any named county. AEP's own report, with an estimated ten minutes and no published response record.
story_contract.closing_answer: A message goes to AEP Texas. The cameras do not prevent fires, and AEP publishes no record of how much sooner anyone arrives.

creative_direction.viewer_question: When a tower camera in west Texas sees smoke, what happens next?
creative_direction.visible_answer: A text bubble lands on a crew phone, a dashed line toward responders stays open and the response record stays blank.

creative_direction.medium_choice: Explanatory animation, mechanism-led. No licensed footage or photograph of an AEP Texas tower or camera feed was found, so original authored illustration performs the sequence AEP describes.
